source.repro: The cut of gbz-cohort-subgraph-cut with one flag changed, `--haplotypes distinct` in place of `--haplotypes all`: `node ~/src/jb2plugins/jbrowse-plugin-graphgenomeviewer/node_modules/@gmod/gbz-base/bin/query.js <hprc-v2.1-mc-grch38.gbz.db> --haplotype-index <anchored.db> --sample GRCh38 --contig <C> --interval <A..B> --context 1000 --snarls --haplotypes distinct --limit 100000 --resolve`, JSON output so each path's `weight` is readable. 'forms' is `paths.length`; 'walks' is the sum of the weights, which counts walk fragments and not distinct haplotypes — it equals the W-line count of gbz-cohort-subgraph-cut at the same locus; 'top weight' is the largest; 'top form steps' and 'median steps' are path-step counts, which exceed distinct nodes wherever a walk revisits one, which is how the top form is shown to be a fragment rather than a walk. Database `https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/human-pangenomics/pangenomes/freeze/release2/minigraph-cactus/v2.1/hprc-v2.1-mc-grch38/hprc-v2.1-mc-grch38.gbz.db`, index `https://jbrowse.org/demos/hprc/hprc-v2.1-mc-grch38.haplotype-index.anchored.db`. Windows as in [[gbz-cohort-subgraph-cut]].
source.notes:
DOES THE GRAPH COLLAPSE A COHORT INTO STRUCTURAL FORMS BY ITSELF. `haplotypes: 'distinct'` merges walks that traverse identical nodes and weights each by how many haplotypes it stands for, which looks like a population readout the graph states for free: a dozen alleles with carrier counts instead of 464 bars.

It is not one. Two walks merge only when every node matches, and at base-level resolution any SNP in the window separates them, so the collapse is weak everywhere and vanishes as the window grows: 464 walks give 395 forms at C4 and the 260 kb CFH window gives 466 forms from 466 walks, every weight 1.

The collapse that does happen is on FRAGMENTS, not on haplotypes, and the two largest weights sit on walks at 9% and 17% of their window's median, while the two loci whose top form is a full-length walk carry weights of 1 and 2. The relation is not monotone across five loci — C4's weight-9 form is 1,574 steps against a 2,331 median — so read it as a warning rather than a law. At CFHR one form carries 97 haplotypes, which looks like the CFHR3/CFHR1 deletion allele at about its known population frequency — and is not: that form's walk is 345 nodes against a median of 3,976, a short piece crossing one end of the window that 97 haplotypes share trivially. Amylase repeats the shape at 203 against 1,217. Where the top form IS a full-length walk, ABCA7 at 3,974 against 3,164 and the CFH window at 10,764 against 10,717, its weight falls to 2 and 1. So a weight is worth nothing without its walk length beside it, and reading one alone invents an allele frequency.

It also costs more than it saves: `distinct` is slower than `all` at every locus and larger in JSON, ABCA7 worst at 126 s.

So a structural-form readout does not come from node identity. Grouping has to happen on a structural tier — the callset's own per-window forms, or the bubble tier — and the graph's role is to give a chosen form its true length.
